title: WHEN THE WORLD FORGETS YOUR SERVICE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then a new king, to whom Joseph meant nothing, came to power in Egypt." - Exodus 1:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One sentence, and everything changes. Joseph had once saved this entire nation from starvation. Egypt owed its survival to him. But a new king came, and to him Joseph meant nothing.

That is the world's memory for you. Human gratitude has a short shelf life. Positions change, management changes, and the good you did last year is quickly forgotten. Many believers have felt this sting — in offices, in ministries, even in families where years of sacrifice go unacknowledged.

But notice what does not change. Pharaoh forgot Joseph; God did not. The favour Israel lost in Egypt's court they never lost in heaven's court.

Jesus warned us not to do good in order to be seen and praised, but promised that the Father who sees in secret will reward (Mt 6:4). Our labour is never wasted, even when it is never noticed.

So serve faithfully today, but do not build your identity on being remembered by people. Build it on being known by God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I serving for recognition or for the Lord?
2. Whose faithful service in my life have I failed to appreciate?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when people forget what I have done, remind me that You never do. Let me serve for Your eyes alone. Amen.
